prompt: There is a speech-sound disorder, not caused by a structural abnormality, for which one symptom is rearranging sounds of a word. The term for the disorder was first defined in 1908 by a German neuroscientist with the first name Hugo. Why was the Nobel Peace Prize given to an American the same year Hugo died?
answer:
The disorder is **apraxia of speech** (also called verbal or speech apraxia). It is associated with the German neurologist **Hugo Liepmann**, who introduced the concept of apraxia in 1908. Affected speakers may make effortful, inconsistent errors, including rearranging sounds within a word.

Liepmann died in **1925**, the year the Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to the American **Charles G. Dawes**—jointly with Austen Chamberlain. Dawes received it for his contribution to resolving Germany’s post–World War I **reparations crisis** and restoring normal economic relations, chiefly through the **Dawes Plan**.
